blocks.text: Testing ka matlab hai code ko alag alag inputs ke saath chala kar dekhna ke woh expectations (umeedon) ke mutabiq kaam karta hai ya nahi. Maqsad yeh hai ke real-world (asal zindagi ke) istemal se pehle problems dhoond kar theek kar liye jayein.

blocks.explanation: Code ke asal istemal se pehle.

blocks.text: Yeh program add function ko test karta hai: function ka result expected (umeed wali) value se milaya jata hai. a, b ya expected badal kar Run karein; expected ghalat ho to FAIL dikhega.

a = 2
b = 3
expected = 5
def add(a, b):
    return a + b
result = add(a, b)
print("add(", a, ",", b, ") =", result)
if result == expected:
    print("Test PASS: result umeed ke mutabiq hai")
else:
    print("Test FAIL: umeed", expected, "thi, mila", result)

blocks.title: Code Explanation (Wazahat)
blocks.text:
"a = 2", "b = 3" aur "expected = 5": do numbers aur woh jawab jis ki hum umeed karte hain (expected value) variables mein rakhe jate hain.
"def add(a, b):" aur "return a + b": add naam ka function banta hai jo dono numbers jor kar jawab wapas (return) karta hai.
"result = add(a, b)": function call hota hai; 2 + 3 = 5 result mein aa jata hai.
"print("add(", a, ",", b, ") =", result)": jawab screen par dikhata hai; commas ki wajah se har hisse ke beech ek space aata hai.
"if result == expected:": compare (muqabla) karta hai ke asal jawab umeed ke barabar hai ya nahi; barabar ho to PASS wali line chalti hai.
"else:": barabar na ho to FAIL wali line chalti hai jo umeed wali value aur asal jawab dono batati hai.
Output: pehli line "add( 2 , 3 ) = 5" aur doosri "Test PASS: result umeed ke mutabiq hai", kyunke 5 aur 5 barabar hain.
Khud try karein: expected = 6 kar ke Run karein: ab "Test FAIL: umeed 6 thi, mila 5" aayega.

items: Testing: alag alag inputs se code chala kar check karna.
